system_description.narrative_title: Global bond rout and rising yields unsettle markets and credit
system_description.narrative_summary: A rapid, broad-based rise in government bond yields — led by US Treasuries — is reshaping expectations for central bank policy, lifting borrowing costs across mortgages, corporate debt and short-term issuance, and transmitting stress into equities, FX and specific real-world projects. Treasuries, Fed hawkishness and stronger growth data act as the primary inputs; markets, bank and corporate balance sheets, housing affordability and political reactions are the principal internal processes and outputs. The system is open: external shocks (oil, global capital flows, geopolitical risk), policy responses (Fed oversight, Treasury issuance) and feedback loops (higher yields -> tighter credit -> economic/political pressure -> policy recalibration) continuously alter the dynamics.
system_description.scope: Within the boundary: sovereign bond markets (especially US Treasuries), interest-rate expectations, central-bank policy signals (Fed), mortgage rate formation and housing-market impact, corporate credit markets and refinancing risk (including large data-centre financings), equity valuations, FX and commodity price interactions that feed into yield moves.
system_description.super_system: Global financial-monetary system / world economy (capital flows, global liquidity and macro policy coordination).
adjacent_subsystems: Corporate investment and project finance (data centres, infrastructure)
Monetary policy and regulatory framework (Fed decisions, bank oversight)
Energy and commodity markets (oil, gold) that influence inflation and yields

variables.name: Sovereign bond yields
variables.description: The prevailing market yields on long- and short-term government debt instruments, measured as continuous yield levels across maturities.

variables.name: Policy rate expectations
variables.description: Market-implied expected path for short-term policy interest rates over relevant horizons.

variables.name: Monetary authority communication tone
variables.description: The intensity and hawkishness/dovishness of official communication about future monetary policy and oversight.

variables.name: Term premium
variables.description: The component of long-term yields reflecting compensation for interest-rate risk and uncertainty over the term structure.

variables.name: Real economic activity growth
variables.description: The rate of change in real output and activity (eg. GDP growth, employment growth) that influences demand and financing conditions.

variables.name: Inflation expectations
variables.description: Market and public expectations for future inflation over short- and long-term horizons.

variables.name: Corporate credit spreads
variables.description: The yield premium on corporate debt over comparable risk-free yields, reflecting perceived default and liquidity risk.

variables.name: Mortgage rate level
variables.description: The average pricing of mortgage borrowing rates for typical loan products, driven by term yields and credit premia.

variables.name: Housing affordability
variables.description: The ratio of household income to housing costs including mortgage payments, reflecting buying power and demand sensitivity.

variables.name: Bank balance-sheet liquidity
variables.description: The available liquid assets and short-term funding buffers held by banks that determine lending capacity and stress tolerance.

variables.name: Debt rollover pressure
variables.description: The flow of upcoming debt maturities and refinancing needs that create periodic funding demand on borrowers and markets.

variables.name: Equity valuation multiples
variables.description: Market valuation metrics (eg. price-to-earnings, EV/EBITDA) that summarize equity price levels relative to fundamentals.

variables.name: Cross-border capital flows
variables.description: Net flows of capital between jurisdictions (portfolio, debt and equity flows) that alter domestic financing conditions.

variables.name: Benchmark currency strength
variables.description: The exchange-value level of a dominant reserve/benchmark currency versus other currencies, affecting external financing and asset prices.

variables.name: Energy price level
variables.description: The prevailing price level for key energy commodities (eg. crude oil) that transmits to inflation and trade balances.

variables.name: Political response pressure
variables.description: The intensity of political and fiscal pressure to alter policy, regulation or issuance in reaction to market and economic stress.

catalysts.title: Upcoming US jobs report
catalysts.description: The next US employment print could materially move Treasury yields and market rate expectations if it surprises on payrolls or wages.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "Why the upcoming jobs report could send 10-year and 30-year Treasury yields surging."

catalysts.title: Near-term US inflation prints
catalysts.description: Upcoming CPI/PCE releases and monthly inflation data could alter inflation expectations and the expected Fed path, shifting long-term yields.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "Week Ahead for FX, Bonds: U.S. Jobs Data in Focus as Another Fed Rate Hike Looks Possible" (inflation data flagged).

catalysts.title: Elevated Fed tightening bias
catalysts.description: Ongoing hawkish communications and regime change at the Fed increase the likelihood of further rate hikes or a prolonged tight stance.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Warsh's regime change at the Fed pushes ahead"; "Another Fed Rate Hike Looks Possible."

catalysts.title: Large US short-term debt issuance
catalysts.description: Planned heavy issuance of short-term Treasury securities (~$1tn) will raise rollover demand and pressure short-end funding markets.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "Wall Street expects US to issue about $1tn of short-term debt as borrowing costs climb."

catalysts.title: Corporate debt maturities pressure
catalysts.description: Large upcoming corporate maturities will test borrowers' refinancing ability, widening credit premia if funding costs remain elevated.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "Corporate debt maturities set to test US borrowers as rates rise."

catalysts.title: Mortgage-rate surge and affordability hit
catalysts.description: Rapid rises in long-term yields have already pushed mortgage rates above 7%, with further increases likely to worsen affordability and housing demand.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Bond rout pushes US mortgage rates past 7%"; "8% mortgage rates are ‘not an impossibility’."

catalysts.title: Near-term oil-price moves
catalysts.description: Oil price retreat or renewed spikes will alter inflation impulses and can ease or reignite bond-market stress.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "Global bond sell-off eases as oil prices retreat from recent highs."

catalysts.title: Foreign capital shift into US equities
catalysts.description: Record flows into US stocks as appetite for debt fades will reduce demand for bonds and exert upward pressure on yields.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "Foreign capital flows into US stocks hit record as appetite for debt fades."

catalysts.title: Texas midterms: data‑center wedge issue

catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Data centre boom emerges as wedge issue in Texas midterms"; Oracle data‑centre pushback coverage.
